title: Patience
definition: Patience is Spirit-formed endurance, restraint, and trust while waiting on God and bearing with others in love.
summary: Patience is Spirit-formed endurance and restraint under delay, difficulty, weakness, provocation, or suffering.
christFocus: Jesus Christ patiently endures with His people and teaches them to wait, forgive, and persevere.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Patience is Spirit-formed endurance with people, circumstances, and God's timing. Scripture calls believers to wait, bear with others, and trust the Lord without giving way to bitterness.

Patience is not passivity or pretending wrong is right. It is faithfulness under delay, weakness, irritation, suffering, and slow growth.

Jesus is patient with weak disciples and slow to anger toward His people. His patience teaches believers how to endure and how to treat others.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because impatience often reveals a demand for control. Patience helps believers endure recovery, suffering, sanctification, caregiving, ministry, and difficult relationships without losing trust in God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Identify where waiting is exposing frustration or unbelief. Pray for endurance, slow your reactions, bear with others gently, and remember how patiently Christ has dealt with you.
